correctness.rationale: Real orthogonal Fourier decomposition of the convolution tensor gives r scalar blocks of amplitude sqrt(n) and (n-r)/2 real complex-multiplication blocks of amplitude sqrt(n/2). Each complex block has real projective norm exactly four from a matching four-term expansion and norm-one self-dual witness. A norm-one injective direct-sum witness matches the sum of block projective costs. The known complex companion follows independently from complex character diagonalization and an injective self-witness. The accompanying finite checks agree, but the proof is independent of enumeration.

originality.rationale: The identical cyclic tensor appears in Prochno (2026), which gives injective and Euclidean norms rather than the real projective norm. Derksen (2015) already gives the complex companion, and Dai–Lim (2022) already gives the two-dimensional real complex-multiplication block norm. The new claim computes the full real group-algebra projective norm for every finite abelian group and its sharp two-torsion-dependent base-field gap. Exact potential equivalences were checked against their actual mathematical implications.
residual_risks: Some earlier real group-algebra or real Wedderburn theory may contain this exact projective-norm formula under a different name.

value.rationale: The precise real nuclear norm is the optimal growth-factor invariant for stable real convolution decompositions. The formula classifies an entire canonical family by group two-torsion, sharply distinguishes groups of the same order (cyclic order-four versus Klein order-four), and explains exactly when complexification changes the best decomposition cost. This is a complete naturally motivated group invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
